requirement:
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap for `requirements.references.outline_comments`. I did not read the implementation. I judged only from the supplied tests and two searches of the tests that reference `coverage.tests` and `authoring_inputs`.

**Run formation and ownership (Rust).** These tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs` cover it:
- **Next-node ownership:** `comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next` checks that consecutive `// one` and `// two` lines both belong to `fn[b]`. `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` adds a run separated from its node by a blank line, a comment inside a function body, and a floating comment before `mod m`, which belongs to `mod[m]`.
- **Trailing comments:** a comment after code on the same line forms its own run and belongs to the innermost node containing that line. `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` checks "trailing second", and `comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node` checks trailing comments after `fn a`, inside `fn b`, and after the closing braces of `fn b` and `mod m`.
- **Comment after another comment:** `a_comment_after_another_comment_on_its_line_forms_its_own_run` checks `/* first */ /* second */`. The first belongs to `fn[b]`, and the second belongs to the root because no node contains that line.
- **Container fallback:** `trailing_comment_after_last_fn_in_mod_belongs_to_the_mod` and `top_level_comment_with_nothing_after_belongs_to_the_root` check that a run with no following node belongs to the container (`mod[m]` or the root). Both "alone in m" and "final" are also checked in the larger test.
- **Run boundaries:** `comment_fences_close_within_one_comment_run` in `src/fenced.rs` shows that consecutive comment lines form one run and a blank line splits runs. A fence opened in one run is not closed by a later run.

**Container binding for Rust inner docs.** `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root` covers `//!` and `/*!` at file level, which belong to the root. `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` covers `//! Module docs.` inside `mod m`. It is followed by a node, `fn inner`, yet it belongs to `mod[m]` and not to `fn[inner]`.

**Other languages.** `comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language` covers Python, TypeScript, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown. The cases include a lead run before a node, a trailing comment, a comment after a container's last node, a nested comment before a node, and a top-level tail owned by the root. `yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one` and `workflow_job_marks_belong_to_the_job_that_follows` in `tests/repository.rs` check YAML ownership on a small case and on the repository's real workflow files.

**Markdown profile.** `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` checks three things. Only the HTML comment block is a comment. The inline `<!-- inline -->` is not inside any comment span. Its line is owned by a `paragraph` node.

**Reference counting for the owner node.** The requirement says a reference counts for its run's owner under the two cited requirements.
- **`coverage.tests`:** `test_functions_need_a_test_reference` in `src/rust_coverage.rs` covers a comment attached above the test, a comment in the body, and closed and unclosed fenced references. It also covers unknown targets and `{cite}`/`{impl}`-only references, which do not count. `tests/coverage.rs` covers the validation-error side.
- **`authoring_inputs`:** `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes` covers the contributed owner node, using a `{fixme}` fence owned by `fn[gap]` and Markdown paragraph owners. `reference_set_digest_tracks_impl_and_test_edges_by_node` checks that a reference moved into a different node changes the digest. `search_returns_innermost_nodes_and_comment_owners` checks a comment match attributed to its owner `fn[after]`.

**Assessment.** The assertions compare exact selectors or owner kinds, so a wrong owner would fail them. The remaining cases, such as a `/*!` block inside a nested module, use the same inner-doc binding that is already tested. The text does not distinguish them as separate obligations.

:::{req} coverage.tests
Every Rust function carrying a test attribute, `#[test]` or an attribute whose
path ends in `test` such as `#[tokio::test]`, including those in Cargo
integration-test targets, MUST carry a `{test}` reference to a requirement or
named example under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`, in a comment
attached to it or within its body. A test function without one MUST be a
validation error naming its file, line, and name.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
MUST contribute the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. A requirement
or example declaration that references the subject with `{impl}` or `{test}`
MUST contribute that complete declaration. For sources outside such declarations,
an `{impl}` reference or `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT contribute source text,
except for structural assessments under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_inputs`;
those sources MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index` and MAY be requested under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`. Sources with only `{cite}` edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `:test:` anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` MUST contribute the complete anchored file,
or for a `path#selector` anchor the anchored node.
An in-source `{test}` reference to the subject MUST contribute the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
An in-source `{fixme}` reference alone MUST NOT contribute the containing source
to the mandatory input set. Its acknowledgment MUST instead be supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs`.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to the assessed subject's direct
references. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
